From cb9e0e5006064a807b5d722c7e3c42f307193792 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Keith Busch <keith.busch@intel.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2019 10:56:43 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] nvme-pci: use blk-mq mapping for unmanaged irqs
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

If a device is providing a single IRQ vector, the IO queue will share
that vector with the admin queue. This is an unmanaged vector, so does
not have a valid PCI IRQ affinity. Avoid trying to extract a managed
affinity in this case and let blk-mq set up the cpu:queue mapping instead.
Otherwise we'd hit the following warning when the device is using MSI:

 Workqueue: nvme-reset-wq nvme_reset_work [nvme]
 RIP: 0010:pci_irq_get_affinity+0x66/0x80

diff --git a/drivers/nvme/host/pci.c b/drivers/nvme/host/pci.c
index 599065ed6a32..f562154551ce 100644
--- a/drivers/nvme/host/pci.c
+++ b/drivers/nvme/host/pci.c
@@ -464,7 +464,7 @@ static int nvme_pci_map_queues(struct blk_mq_tag_set *set)
 		 * affinity), so use the regular blk-mq cpu mapping
 		 */
 		map->queue_offset = qoff;
-		if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL)
+		if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL && offset)
 			blk_mq_pci_map_queues(map, to_pci_dev(dev->dev), offset);
 		else
 			blk_mq_map_queues(map);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/nvme/host/pci.c`**
   - The condition in the `if` statement at line 464 was modified. The original condition checked if `i` was not equal to `HCTX_TYPE_POLL`. The modified condition adds an additional check for `offset`, making it `if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL && offset)`.
   - This change affects how the function `blk_mq_pci_map_queues` is called. It will now only call `blk_mq_pci_map_queues` if both conditions are satisfied, otherwise it will call `blk_mq_map_queues`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `pci.c` is aimed at improving the handling of IRQ vectors for NVMe devices that use a single IRQ vector. By adding the check for `offset`, the code ensures that the mapping of queues is only performed when it is appropriate, thus preventing potential warnings related to unmanaged IRQs. This change is directly related to the issue described in the patch, which is to avoid extracting a managed affinity for unmanaged IRQs and to allow the block-mq subsystem to handle the CPU-to-queue mapping correctly.

        Root cause:
        The bug arises from attempting to extract a managed IRQ affinity for a single unmanaged IRQ vector provided by the device. This leads to a warning when the device is using Message Signaled Interrupts (MSI), as the system cannot determine a valid PCI IRQ affinity for the shared vector between the IO queue and the admin queue. The modification ensures that the blk-mq subsystem handles the CPU-to-queue mapping instead, preventing the warning.

Fixes: 22b5560195bd6 ("nvme-pci: Separate IO and admin queue IRQ vectors")
Reported-by: Iván Chavero <ichavero@chavero.com.mx>
Reviewed-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Keith Busch <keith.busch@intel.com>  
        
        Patch:
         
 static int nvme_pci_map_queues(struct blk_mq_tag_set *set)
 {
 	struct nvme_dev *dev = set->driver_data;
 	int i, qoff, offset;
 
 	offset = queue_irq_offset(dev);
 	for (i = 0, qoff = 0; i < set->nr_maps; i++) {
 		struct blk_mq_queue_map *map = &set->map[i];
 
 		map->nr_queues = dev->io_queues[i];
 		if (!map->nr_queues) {
 			BUG_ON(i == HCTX_TYPE_DEFAULT);
 			continue;
 		}
 
 		/*
 		 * The poll queue(s) doesn't have an IRQ (and hence IRQ
 		 * affinity), so use the regular blk-mq cpu mapping
 		 */
 		map->queue_offset = qoff;
-		if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL)
+		if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL && offset)
 			blk_mq_pci_map_queues(map, to_pci_dev(dev->dev), offset);
 		else
 			blk_mq_map_queues(map);
 		qoff += map->nr_queues;
 		offset += map->nr_queues;
 	}
 
 	return 0;
 }
